boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Haverford rituals and recurring student practices, from arrival through graduation.

cards.title: Customs
cards.subtitle: Haverford’s yearlong first-year experience
cards.notes: If you are a new student, use your Customs group and its student leaders to learn campus resources, community expectations, and Haverford history.
cards.short_summary: An orientation and first-year program with roots in Haverford’s earliest student customs.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford describes Customs as arguably its oldest tradition, with roots in the mid-1800s, and now runs it as a yearlong first-year program.
cards.access_notes: For incoming students; the College notes that updated Class of 2030 information will be available in early June 2026.

cards.title: Customs Week
cards.subtitle: Five-day welcome week before fall semester
cards.notes: Incoming students should follow the assigned Customs Week schedule, meet their hall group, and use the sessions to begin learning student self-governance.
cards.short_summary: The required opening-week portion of Haverford’s Customs experience.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford calls Customs Week a five-day orientation and welcome week immediately before fall semester and says it is required for incoming students.
cards.access_notes: For incoming students; schedule information is issued by the Customs program.

cards.title: Sign the Honor Code
cards.subtitle: A Customs milestone for new students
cards.notes: During Customs, read the current student-authored Code carefully and treat the signing as a commitment to its trust, concern, and respect framework.
cards.short_summary: New students sign the Code during their Customs arrival period.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford Magazine reports that new students sign the Honor Code during Customs in late August.
cards.access_notes: Participation is part of the new-student Customs experience.

cards.title: Fall Plenary
cards.subtitle: Student-body gathering each fall
cards.notes: Attend when eligible, help establish quorum, and use the discussion and voting process to engage with the student-governance agenda.
cards.short_summary: One of Haverford’s twice-yearly student-body Plenary meetings.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford Students’ Council states that Plenary occurs twice each school year and that the fall gathering focuses on ratifying the alcohol policy.
cards.access_notes: For enrolled students; Plenary requires at least two-thirds of the student body for quorum.

cards.title: Spring Plenary
cards.subtitle: Student-body gathering each spring
cards.notes: Attend when eligible, review proposed resolutions, and take part in the student-led process that approves the Honor Code.
cards.short_summary: The spring Plenary centers on approval of the Honor Code.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford Students’ Council states that Spring Plenary centers on approving the Honor Code and requires a two-thirds student-body quorum.
cards.access_notes: For enrolled students; consult Students’ Council for the meeting agenda and resolutions.

cards.title: Declare Your Major Out Loud
cards.subtitle: Outside the VCAM facility each spring
cards.notes: Sophomores invited to declare can step to the microphone outside VCAM and announce their chosen major during the spring gathering.
cards.short_summary: A newer ceremony where sophomores publicly announce their majors, accompanied by cowbells.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford Magazine documents a spring tradition in which sophomores declare their chosen major at a microphone outside VCAM, with miniature cowbells.
cards.access_notes: The article says sophomores are invited each spring; participation is optional.

cards.title: Add Your Name to the Cupola
cards.subtitle: Founders Hall graduation tradition
cards.notes: Graduating seniors can join the documented pre-Commencement ritual of adding their names to the collected autographs in Founders Hall’s cupola.
cards.short_summary: Seniors leave their signatures in the Founders Hall cupola before Commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford reports that the Class of 2026 marked the end of their time at the College by adding names to the autographs in Founders Hall’s cupola.
cards.source_title: Ready to Bloom: Commencement 2026 | Haverford College
cards.access_notes: A graduation-period tradition for seniors; follow College instructions for cupola access.

cards.title: Toll the Founders Bell
cards.subtitle: Founders Hall cupola, near Commencement
cards.notes: Graduating seniors may take part in the long-running bell-tolling tradition after completing their studies and before Commencement.
cards.short_summary: A senior milestone paired with signing the Founders Hall cupola.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford states that graduating seniors have long added their names to the cupola and tolled its bell as they finish their College experience.
cards.source_title: Ready to Bloom: Commencement 2026 | Haverford College
cards.access_notes: For graduating seniors; rooftop access has mobility challenges, and the College now offers a ground-level bell option.

cards.title: Ring In Your Arrival
cards.subtitle: Ground-level bell adjacent to Founders Hall
cards.notes: After Convocation, first-year students can ring the ground-level brass bell to mark their arrival in the Haverford community.
cards.short_summary: A new arrival ritual tied to the Honor Code’s three pillars.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford says student leaders created a new tradition in which first-year students ring the brass bell after Convocation to mark their arrival.
cards.source_title: Ringing in a New Tradition | Haverford College
cards.access_notes: The bell is ground-level beside Founders Hall; the article identifies the ritual as following Convocation.

cards.title: Take Home Your First-Year Plant
cards.subtitle: Haverford College Arboretum greenhouse tradition
cards.notes: First-year students can ask the Arboretum about the customary plant and use its care support to keep it going through college breaks.
cards.short_summary: For decades, incoming students have received a free plant as an introduction to the Arboretum.
cards.evidence_claim: Haverford reports that the Arboretum has given every incoming student a free plant as an introduction to the Arboretum for more than 35 years.
cards.access_notes: Ask Arboretum staff about current first-year distribution and plant-care options.
